requirements.description: R2 BLOCK only for an HMA-reproduced kernel violation; unwaivable
R3 WAIVABLE only for a measured budget excess
R4 report cannot create, suppress or clear BLOCK/WAIVABLE
R5 failed criterion check creates no finding
R7 unresolved BLOCK/WAIVABLE blocks gate and closure
R8 waiver scoped to the exact finding and artifact

findings.title: A finding waiver survives a change of the measured artifact
findings.diagnosis: requireFindingsResolved looks up ActiveWaivers by finding id only; HMA re-raises HMA-BUDGET-<name> under the same id for every new artifact; no waiver ever expires automatically. A waiver granted for a 4-file change passed the review->verification gate for a 25-file change after a new implementation and approving review.

evidence.observation: gate passes: 25 files vs budget 3 under the 4-file waiver

fix.action: Bind a waiver of an HMA-established finding to the reviewed artifact: require the waiver operation to carry head and diff_digest and compare them (or the review artifact digest) with the current reviewed artifact in requireFindingsResolved; otherwise treat the WAIVABLE as unwaived.
fix.why: Architecture 7.2: a waiver expires when its scoped artifacts change; a human must see a new excess.

verification.method: Run B1 re-review path with a bound waiver on the same artifact

fix.tradeoffs: Waivers for HMA findings must then always bind head/diff; every new artifact needs a new waiver.
fix.alternative: Put the review artifact digest into the established finding (id suffix or a field) so a new artifact is a new finding.

findings.title: A waiver cannot take effect at the review gate without a fresh independent review
findings.diagnosis: The waiver operation is a core record after the review; requireOnlyOwnSnapshotsSince accepts only findings snapshots, so the gate refuses HOST_CORE_BINDING_STALE. Only a new packet, review and import (which re-raises the same id) lets the waiver count. Shipped tests check requireFindingsResolved only, never the gate after a waiver.

evidence.observation: any non-snapshot record after the review is stale
gate after waiver: HOST_CORE_BINDING_STALE; after re-review: pass

fix.action: Allow KindWaiverOperation GRANT records scoped to a finding of this unit after the review in requireOnlyOwnSnapshotsSince, or document and test the re-review requirement as the waiver path.
fix.why: A human waiver is the architecture's resolution of a WAIVABLE (5.2); it should not cost a second independent review.

verification.expected: gate passes after the waiver without re-review

fix.tradeoffs: Accepting waiver records after the review widens the stale-binding allowlist; with N1 fixed the waiver is artifact-bound, so the risk is bounded.
fix.alternative: Keep the refusal and make the re-review the documented path, with a gate-level test.

findings.title: Dirty-target measurement follows untracked symlinks: FIFO hang, outside files read
findings.diagnosis: measureChange reads every untracked path with os.ReadFile, which follows symlinks and has no size or time bound. An untracked symlink to a FIFO blocks findings import indefinitely while the host run lock is held; a symlink to a 5000-line file outside the repository counts 5000 lines (git counts the committed symlink as 1 line). A symlink to /dev/zero would grow memory without bound (inferred, not run).

fix.action: Lstat each untracked path: count a symlink as git does (its link text, one line), skip or refuse non-regular files, and stream-count newlines from regular files with a byte cap (stop once the budget is exceeded).
fix.why: The measurement must be bounded, repository-local and consistent with the committed-path count.

verification.method: Run B10 fifo and symlink cases

fix.tradeoffs: A capped count reports 'exceeded' rather than an exact number.
fix.alternative: Refuse findings import when an untracked non-regular path exists.

findings.title: Human override can downgrade an HMA-measured WAIVABLE to ADVISORY
findings.diagnosis: EvaluateResolution refuses overrides of BLOCK only. hma resolve accepted WAIVABLE->ADVISORY for U1/HMA-BUDGET-max_files; the closure-form findings check then passes with no waiver, so a run could close VERIFIED_SUCCESS with a measured excess. The review gate is not bypassable (stale binding, then re-raise). Closure is latent: the core refuses verified outcomes today.

fix.action: Decide (Lennon) whether a WAIVABLE may be overridden. Recommended: refuse FindingOverride for ids whose source part starts with HMA- (new reason), so an HMA fact is resolved only by waiver or correction.
fix.why: Architecture 7.2 keeps waivers visible and forbids VERIFIED_SUCCESS with one; an override hides the excess.

verification.expected: override refused, or closure check still refuses

fix.tradeoffs: Removes a human shortcut for HMA findings only.
fix.alternative: Have requireFindingsResolved ignore overrides for HMA- findings.

findings.title: no_shell resolves the plan executable differently from the capture
findings.diagnosis: lookPathAbs ignores the executable bit and joins names containing '/' with PATH entries; capture's resolveExecutable uses exec.LookPath and refuses relative paths. A non-executable '#!/bin/sh' file named true earlier on PATH makes plan command 'true' an unwaivable BLOCK although the capture runs /usr/bin/true.

fix.action: Export and reuse the capture's resolveExecutable; on a resolution error apply RejectShell to the name only.
fix.why: The kernel fact must be the capture's own policy decision.

findings.title: Live config can over-count (and run a clean filter) in the dirty measurement
findings.diagnosis: With .git/info/attributes '* filter=x' and filter.x.clean in .git/config, the dirty measurement went from 4 to 2001 lines (and to 1 with an emptying filter); the filter command runs. The handoff says this exposure can only under-count; it can also over-count, giving a false WAIVABLE (never a BLOCK).

fix.action: Correct the stated limit, or measure dirty content without filters (hash worktree files with hash-object --no-filters into a temporary index and diff base against that tree).
fix.why: Truthful limits; same D5a live-config class.
fix.tradeoffs: The temporary-index approach is more code.
fix.alternative: Accept under the trusted-host model with corrected wording.

findings.title: Closure findings check allows VERIFIED_SUCCESS while a waiver is active
findings.diagnosis: After a waiver, VERIFIED_SUCCESS passes requireFindingsResolved. Model validation checks only the terminal record's own Waivers, not the chain's active waiver operations. Latent: core refuses verified outcomes today.

evidence.observation: VERIFIED_SUCCESS waived passes the findings check

fix.action: In the closure branch refuse VERIFIED_SUCCESS when ProjectResolutionState(core).ActiveWaivers is non-empty.

verification.expected: VERIFIED_SUCCESS refused after a waiver; VERIFIED_WITH_WAIVERS reaches credit

fix.alternative: Defer to the closure gate work, recorded explicitly.

findings.title: A native (legacy-manual) review never computes HMA facts
findings.diagnosis: findingFacts runs only in findings import. In a run with no review packet, EvaluateReview accepts a native APPROVE and the review gate checks only recorded findings, so a budget excess or shell plan command passes review->verification. Credit still needs an imported review, so verified closure stays blocked.

evidence.observation: native review allowed when no packet exists

fix.action: Refuse native review in a run with a lease plan, or compute the facts at the review gate.
fix.why: The D5b guarantees should not depend on the review mode.

verification.method: Native-review control in a plan run

fix.tradeoffs: May break legacy hosts that hold plans.

findings.title: Measurement definitions under- and over-count by design
findings.diagnosis: A pure 60-line rename counts 2 files and 120 lines; a 1 MiB binary or one-line file counts 1 line; untracked files ignored only via .git/info/exclude are counted (consistent with repostate). Wrappers such as find or timeout in a plan command are an unwaivable no_shell BLOCK, consistent with the capture policy.

fix.action: Document the definitions in the plan contract, or count renames once.
fix.why: Planners need to know what the budget measures.

limitations: Same vendor family as implementer (Claude Sonnet 5.5; auditor Claude Opus 5.5); no provider separation
Isolation partial: fresh context, but the closure input is the auditor's own prior report and the dispatch describes the fixes
Closure path checked only up to the findings check; the core refuses verified outcomes (OUTCOME_NOT_IMPLEMENTED)
N8 not run: no native-review fixture with a lease plan exists
/dev/zero symlink case inferred, not run (would exhaust memory)
Merges and submodules checked by code reading only
